title: C: bounded grants and committed receive intervals
description:
Extend lichen/subsys/lichen/link/tdma.c and its link.h/link_ctx.h public state with bounded owner-qualified grants and receive commitments. TX eligibility requires the sender's valid grant and the next-hop receiver's compatible opportunity on the same physical channel/profile. Prevent half-duplex overlaps and preemption of committed RX by newly queued urgent traffic. Candidate hashes and anonymous slot maps remain nonexclusive.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: This is b7z9.22's C CCP2 integration slice. Reuse oamc's closed slot-map gate/writer and existing validators rather than reimplement them or add an old-roll-up edge. Keep source, headers and shims synchronized, with no dynamic hot-path allocation. No per-packet reservation exchange, universal link ACK, queue expansion, custody-policy change, identity migration or OSCORE/EDHOC modification is introduced.
acceptance_criteria: Consume vectors.04/.08 through production C eligibility with independent event traces. Cover wrong/absent grant owner, missing receiver RX, RX/TX overlap, expiry, channel/profile mismatch, queued SOS during RX, zero slots and persistent equal hash residues through wrap. Extend lichen/tests/ccp_slot_map and lichen/tests/tdma_guard_budget, keeping assertions and ASan/UBSan active. Run scoped C lint and header/native compile checks on local Linux/heft using the manifest-qualified toolchain; no device access.
